terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: Not solved; review camera is fixed by the consumer harness.

objectClass.primaryType: 3-candy cluster of maple-leaf-shaped maple sugar candies
objectClass.notes: Matte faceted clay shading, flat color facets only. Identity carried ENTIRELY by silhouette (5-lobed leaf outline) since color cannot distinguish this from chestnut/cinnamon in the same batch -- the batch's flagged hardest legibility case (CRIB.md).

reasoning: Three near-identical candy assemblies, each rim+body, so componentCount scores 2 (matching blueberry's body+crown scale, not choco/cranberry's flat mesh=1 bodies).

Silhouette scores 3 (highest in this sub-batch): 10-point non-circular outline with 5 asymmetric lobes and a deep stem-notch is the batch's most structurally involved silhouette -- more than redbean's near-spherical mound.
hierarchyDepth scores 2: each candy has a real meso-level plateau child (vein crease), one level deeper than a flat single-mesh body.
materialLayerCount scores 1: 2 buckets (rim + body), same scale as olive/blueberry/redbean precedent.
Local detail density scores 2: rim/plateau height step + 5-spoke vein crease are two distinct authored details.
Occlusion risk scores 1: candies overlap only at their bases (per reference), no lobe is fully hidden by another candy from the fixed camera.
Action readiness scores 0: static turntable showcase prop.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Simple tier by part count, but needs meso depth (plateau child) and material local overrides (rim-is-real-step rationale) unlike choco/cranberry's flatter mesh=1 budget.

detailInventory.note: Enumerated by hand from the three supplied reference views -- CRIB.md skip rule for single-repeated-system objects.

details.observation: 5-lobed maple leaf outline (1 main + 2 upper-side + 2 basal tips, deep stem-notch valley at the bottom) is the sole feature distinguishing this from chestnut or cinnamon in the same batch -- color alone cannot.
details.inference: Maple-leaf-shaped sugar candy, per prompt subject.

details.observation: The cream border is genuinely proud of the darker inner plateau (real height step, consistent shading discontinuity across all views), not a flat 2-color paint job.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

mustMatch: 5-lobed maple leaf silhouette, distinct from chestnut/cinnamon
2-tone rim/plateau color read (flat, no height step -- see risk bevel-wall-dropped-for-rendering-bug)
faceted flat shading baked into geometry
niceToHave: exact real-maple branching vein topology (simplified to 5 spokes here)

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.name: 5-lobed maple leaf silhouette reads clearly, distinct from chestnut/cinnamon
Rim/plateau 2-tier step reads via shading, not just flat color
Leaf lobe shape survives 64px thumbnail downsample

sculptPipeline.blockedReason: blockout requires a browser screenshot and self-correction review before structural-pass unlocks
nextRequiredEvidence: blockout browser render screenshot from your agent's browser/screenshot tool
AI vision score >= 0.7 with layer scores and mismatch critique
critical semantic feature scores from the same image pair meeting their individual thresholds
reviewHistory entry for blockout with action=continue

droppedPasses.lighting-pass: lighting is fixed by the consumer harness and is not authorable in the model
droppedPasses.interaction-pass: static showcase prop with no sockets, hinges or colliders beyond a bounding proxy

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: Consumer runtime keeps only map and color; repo bans PBR maps outright.

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold

lightingPass.authority: Lighting is fixed by the consumer: scripts/breadlab.ts mirrors scripts/thumbsHarness.ts with a warm directional key 0xffe2b0 at (-2, 6, 2) intensity 1.4, an ambient 0xfff0dc at 0.75 and a cool fill 0xdce8ff at (2.5, 3, -2) intensity 0.2.
mustAvoid: relying on a contact shadow the harness does not render

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: The runtime normalizes the cluster's longest axis to 1.6, so absolute dimensions are arbitrary.

The true maple leaf vein topology (1 midrib + branching side veins) is simplified to 5 independent center-to-tip spokes -- a deliberate low-poly stylization documented as a niceToHave gap, not a measurement error.

The reference's small stem nub below the leaf's bottom point (visible faintly in maple-2.png) is NOT modeled -- omitted as a budget/legibility tradeoff, same class of honest omission as redbean's inner spiral curl.

coordinateFrame.front: +Z, the direction the harness three-quarter camera at (-1.6, 2.2, 2.6) looks from
coordinateFrame.scaleReference: LEAF_RADIUS = 0.42 relative unit. Absolute scale is meaningless: the consumer runtime refits the cluster's longest axis to 1.6 (types.ts section 6).

silhouette.boundingShape: 3 flat leaf-shaped candies loosely overlapping at their bases, roughly 1.7 wide by 0.11 tall by 1.3 deep in relative units

aspectRatios.source: maple-3.png -- main tip radius 1.0 vs basal tip radius 0.58

silhouette.symmetry: each candy is mirror-symmetric about its own main-tip axis; the 3-candy cluster as a whole is asymmetric
dominantCurves: flat leaf-shaped extrusion, no curvature -- entirely faceted planar surfaces
negativeSpaces: deep stem-notch valley at the bottom of each leaf, between the 2 basal tips
4 shallower valley sinuses between the other lobe pairs
landmarks: 5-lobed leaf outline is the sole identity carrier -- color cannot distinguish this from chestnut/cinnamon in the same batch

observations: 3 maple-leaf-shaped candies resting flat, loosely overlapping at their bases in a triangular cluster
each candy is a classic 5-lobed maple leaf outline: 1 large main tip, 2 medium upper-side tips, 2 smaller basal tips, deep V stem-notch at the bottom between the basal tips
originally modeled with a real geometric 2-tier rim/plateau step (see spec risk bevel-wall-dropped-for-rendering-bug for why this was simplified to a single flat top height, color-only 2-tone)
the inner plateau carries a central-vein-to-each-tip crease pattern, darker where sunk, lighter on the raised facets between veins
visible side-wall thickness at each candy's lower edge confirms real extrusion, not a flat cutout
rim band width is a substantial fraction of the half-radius, not a hairline border
side wall (candy thickness) clearly visible at the bottom edge of each leaf, same cream tone as the rim
confirms the 5-lobe outline and deep stem-notch precisely
all 3 candies lie flat, none tilted on-edge -- the fixed 3/4 hero camera reveals edge thickness through perspective alone

componentTree.name: Maple candy inner plateau (1)
componentTree.topologyRationale: Inner plateau fan (same height as the rim, TOP_Y -- no bevel step, see risk bevel-wall-dropped-for-rendering-bug) plus the flat bottom cap, both flat color. localOverrides.description: Unlike a flat 2-color leaf, the reference shows the rim genuinely PROUD of the recessed inner plateau (TOP_Y > TOP_Y) -- confirmed by consistent shading discontinuity at the boundary across all 3 candies and all 3 reference views, not just a flat color line.

Never set flatShading: that flag is not inherited by the runtime swap either. Faceting must be baked as split vertices.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Team-lead-assigned cluster-group budget for this batch (300-700 tri target, <=68KB target, types.ts R2 hard ceiling <=2500 tri/<=100KB). Per candy: rim=40tri (20 top band + 20 side wall, bevel wall dropped -- see risk), plateau=20tri (5-spoke crease split), bottom cap=10tri = 70tri/candy x 3 = 210tri by construction. Deliberately below the 300 floor -- thin detail-driven asset, CRIB.md explicitly allows undershoot when legibility is the limiter, not triangle count.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: Warm directional key 0xffe2b0 at (-2, 6, 2), intensity 1.4, upper-left.
lightingFromPhoto.exposure: no exposure control, no tone mapping.

proceduralStrategy: Build a custom indexed prism per candy from the 10-point outline: outer-top ring (TOP_Y) -> inner-top ring (TOP_Y, scaled INNER_SCALE) -> rim-top band; outer-top ring -> outer-bottom ring (BOTTOM_Y) -> side wall (both bands = maple-rim material). No bevel wall -- rim-top and plateau meet at the SAME height, TOP_Y (dropped post-implementation, see risk bevel-wall-dropped-for-rendering-bug).

Inner plateau fan (center at TOP_Y to the inner ring) with 5 vein-mid vertices splitting each of the 10 base fan triangles at its tip-adjacent center edge (chestnut.ts CREASE generalized). Flat bottom cap fan (center at BOTTOM_Y to outer-bottom ring), no vein detail (hidden underside). Both = maple-body material.

Winding verified per band via cross-product sign (cheese.ts's U x V = N method): rim-top band and inner-plateau fan need +Y normals (reversed CCW-by-angle order); bottom cap needs -Y (natural CCW-by-angle order); side wall reuses buildRevolvedShell's proven a0/b0 ring-transition index pattern for outward normals.

No jitter anywhere (JITTER_AMP=0, R4) -- thin pointed lobes at this poly budget cannot absorb even a small random perturbation without losing tip sharpness (same class of exception as cheese's box-corner jitter-skip).

sliceTriangles(0, 40) for the rim bucket, (40, 70) for the body bucket per candy (continuous-range split by construction order, never a vertex mask) -- then top-planar UV per bucket, merge all 3 candies' matching buckets across instances into exactly 2 meshes.

No lay-down rotation -- all 3 candies rest flat, local Y is world Y directly. Independent XZ offset + yaw per instance; no per-instance floor correction needed since the prism's own bottom is already flat at BOTTOM_Y for every instance (shared ground plane by construction, unlike olive's per-instance bbox snap).
animationAnchors: root pivot supports whole-cluster rotation for the showcase turntable
each candy is a named instance
destructionAnchors: each candy is its own fractureGroup; the only plausible break is one candy sliding away from the cluster

risks.description: assets/prompts/ingredients/maple.json names a vein-groove hex (#8F6224) and a raised-facet highlight hex (#D9A85C) this spec does not paint as separate materials.
risks.mitigation: Covered by the plateau's own vein-crease geometry (dark inside the crease from its own facet normals, lit on the raised facets between veins via free N.L falloff), same drop logic as olive/chestnut/redbean body precedent.

risks.description: CRIB.md flags maple as the batch's hardest legibility case: 5 thin pointed lobes with deep sinuses risk merging into a blob at the 64px thumbnail target, same failure mode cranberry hit before its instance count was cut from 6 to 3.
risks.mitigation: Kept lobes bold (basal-tip radius 0.58 vs main-tip 1.0, not razor-thin) and valleys deep (bottom stem-notch at 0.20) per CRIB's 'make the leaf big, cut the count' guidance. Verify honestly at 64px (LANCZOS downsample onto card bg) before declaring pass; if it fails, the fallback is reducing the cluster from 3 candies to 2 (documented in CRIB as an acceptable batch-4 outcome), not adding more triangles.

risks.description: Any vertex-color-based region paint is silently discarded by the runtime's MeshLambertMaterial swap.
risks.mitigation: Only 2 materials total, each covering whole contiguous triangle ranges (rim / body) by construction order; no vertexPaint block is authored anywhere in this spec.

risks.description: A flatShading flag is not inherited by the runtime material swap.
risks.mitigation: Faceting is baked into geometry by splitting vertices (scripts/breads/lib.ts facet) before export.

risks.description: This is the batch's only fully hand-built (non-buildRevolvedShell) indexed geometry with several distinct band/fan types, each needing manually-verified winding -- a single flipped band would render as a hole (backface-culled), not a subtle visual bug.
risks.mitigation: Each band's winding was derived analytically via cross-product sign before implementation (documented in proceduralStrategy), not guessed; render inspection (missing/black faces) is the fast empirical check if one band is still wrong.

risks.description: The originally-implemented 3-ring rim/bevel/plateau structure (R1 outer-top -> R2 inner-top -> R3 inner-plateau, a real proud-rim height step matching the reference) punched a background-colored hole through near whichever tip faced the harness camera, on every one of the 3 candies, across multiple independent redesigns of the crease/vein logic. Root cause NOT fully determined: DoubleSide materials ruled out backface culling, an exhaustive triangle-area check found zero degenerate triangles, and cross-product sign verification found all 3 bands (rim-top, bevel, side wall) correctly wound on all 10 segments each -- yet isolating rim-top-alone and (rim-top+bevel+side, no plateau) both rendered perfectly clean, while adding the plateau back (with or without the vein split) reintroduced the hole every time. Doubling the bevel's height (0.02 -> 0.045) did not fix it either, ruling out sub-pixel wall thinness.
risks.mitigation: Collapsed the 3-ring structure to 2 rings sharing one height (TOP_Y) -- rim-top band and plateau fan now meet directly with no bevel wall in between. This is the exact construct present in every failing configuration; removing it eliminated the hole in the hero shot, all 3 azimuth shots, and the roundtrip parity shot. Traded the reference's genuine raised-rim 3D relief for a flat 2-tone color split (still 2 materials, still matches the leaf's overall look) in exchange for a verified-clean render. Flagged for the delegating session: if the raised-rim look is later wanted, budget a fresh investigation rather than reintroducing this exact 3-ring pattern blind.
